Rashi on Nedarim 49b:10:1.hebrew: אי כמלוי ברבית כו' - שהן מרויחין ביותר, ופניהן צהובין ויפין:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:10:1.english: Either like usurers, etc. - For they profit greatly, and their faces are radiant and handsome.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:10:2.hebrew: תרוייהו - לגדל חזירין ולהלוות ברבית אסירי ליהודאי. ודאי לאו מינייהו פני צהובין:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:10:2.english: Both of them - Raising pigs and lending with interest are prohibited to Jews. Certainly it is not from them [that] my face is radiant.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:11:1.english: [He] would carry a pitcher - He would carry the pitcher to the study hall to sit on it.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:11:2.english: Labor that brings honor [to its master], etc. - For now he will sit upon it in the study hall.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:12:1.english: She went out, took wool - She went out to the market, bought wool, and made a cloak.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:12:2.english: Dehutevei - And she made from it [the wool] a good cloak.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:12:3.hebrew: וכד נפקת - איהי לשוקא, הות ניכסי ביה:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:12:3.english: And when she would go out - she [would go out] to the market, she would cover herself with it.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:12:4.hebrew: ורבי יהודה כד הוה מצלי, הוה נמי מכסי ביה:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:12:4.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, when he would pray, would also cover himself with it.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:12:5.english: Who wrapped me in a coat - For it was so dear to them, as they did not have another [garment].

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:1:1.english: We pray for the sick - [In the blessing,] "Who heals the sick of His people Israel."

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:1:2.english: The suffering - For the remnant of their scribes.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:2:1.english: Our Mishnah - Which teaches that thick [cooked food] is not eaten with bread.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:2:2.english: Not in accordance with the Babylonians - For they eat their bread with porridge [as a relish], which is thick.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:3:1.english: Fastidious ones - [People who are] meticulous about food.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:3:2.english: [How is it best] - With which thing is eating the porridge best?

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:3:3.hebrew: דחיטי - יכול לאכלה בלחם של חטים, ודייסא דשערי יכול לאכלה בלחם של שעורים:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:3:3.english: [Porridge] of wheat - Can one eat it with wheat bread, and barley porridge — can one eat it with barley bread?

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:3:4.hebrew: או דילמא - דייסא של חטים יפה לאכול בשל שעורים, ושל שעורים בשל חטים. ואית דגרסי נקרני, מלשון כי קרן עור פניו (שמות ל״ד:כ״ט), מלאים חכמה ומאירה פניהם, שנא' חכמת אדם תאיר פניו:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:3:4.english: Or perhaps - wheat porridge is good to eat with barley [bread], and barley [porridge] with wheat [bread]. And some read "nakranei" — from the expression "for the skin of his face shone [karan]" (Exodus 34:29) — [meaning] full of wisdom and their faces shine, as it is stated: "A man's wisdom makes his face shine."

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:4:1.hebrew: אכלה בחסיסי - היה מלפת פיתו בחסיסי, ומפרש לה במסכת פסחים (דף לט:): קימחא דאבישונא — קמח של קליות שעורים שלא הביאו שליש, ומיבשין אותן בתנור, וקלופין הן:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:4:1.english: He ate it with chasisei - He would eat his bread with chasisei [as a relish], and it is explained in Tractate Pesachim (39b): kimcha d'avishuna — [which is] flour of toasted barley [kernels] that have not [yet] reached a third [of their growth], and they dry them in an oven, and they are hulled.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:5:1.hebrew: מזמני לך לאכל דייסא עד פרסה - דע שאותו מאכל איכו סועד לבך אלא עד הילוך פרסה. ובשר השור עד שלש פרסאות: ע"א: אי מזמני לך לאכול דייסא עד פרסה, לך אחר דייסא לאכול, וטפי לא; ולאכול בשר שור, לך עד שלש פרסאות:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:5:1.english: [If] they invite you to eat porridge up to a parasang - Know that that food does not sustain your heart except for a walk of a parasang, and ox meat [sustains it] up to three parasangs. Another interpretation: If they invite you to eat porridge up to a parasang, go after porridge to eat [it], and no more; and to eat ox meat, go up to three parasangs.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:5:2.hebrew: כל מידעם לא תפלוט קמי רבך - לא תרוק רוק בפני רבך, כדאמר במס' עירובין (דף צט.): הרק לפני רבו חייב מיתה, שנאמר "וכל משנאי אהבו מות". אבל אם אכלת דלעת ודייסא ונזדמן לך הרוק בפיך, פלוט בפני רבך וזרוק אותו לחוץ, שיש בו סכנת נפשות, שהן קשין לגופו של אדם כפתילה של אבר:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:5:2.english: Do not spit out anything before your teacher - Do not spit spittle before your teacher, as it is stated in Tractate Eruvin (99a): "One who spits before his teacher is liable to death, as it is stated: 'And all who hate Me love death.'" However, if you ate gourd or porridge and spittle happens [to gather] in your mouth, spit before your teacher and cast it outside, for there is mortal danger in it, as they are as harmful to a person's body as a lead wick.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:5:3.english: And even before King Shapur, spit [it] out - And do not be embarrassed.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:6:1.english: Your filth - [The] dirt that is in his fingernails.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:6:2.hebrew: עד מתי אתה מאכילני רוקך - שהיה נותן ההוצא בפיו, ומדביק בו הרוק שבפיו, ומחזירו בקערה:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:6:2.english: For how long will you feed me your spittle - For he would put the hutza [fork] into his mouth, and stick the spittle in his mouth onto it, and return it to the bowl.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:7:2.english: Since they do not leave the intestines.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:7:3.hebrew: כ"ש - דמעלו, שנסמוך עליהן, שאין אנו צריכים לאכול מאכל אחר למחר:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:7:3.english: All the more so - that they are beneficial, that we can rely on them, [meaning] that we do not need to eat other food tomorrow.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:9:1.hebrew: מורה ורוי - אתה תלמיד בעל הוראה ואתה שיכור, מפני שהיו פניו צהובין כל שעה:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:9:1.english: A teacher and a drunk - [Are] you a scholar, a master of instruction, and you [are] a drunkard? [She said this] because his face was radiant at all times.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:9:2.english: Trustworthiness in the hands of that woman - My trustworthiness [is] in your hands, that I do not drink wine the entire year except [for] kiddush and havdala.

Rashi on Nedarim 49b:9:3.hebrew: וחוגר אני צדעי - וקושר אני צדעי, פדחתי, משום מיחוש ראשי מפני ד' כוסות ששתיתי, שאני חושש מהן מפסח עד עצרת:
Rashi on Nedarim 49b:9:3.english: And I tie my temples - And I bind my temples — my forehead — because of a headache from the four cups that I drank, from which I suffer from Passover until Atzeret [Shavuot].

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:11:1.english: He would carry a pitcher - to sit [on it] in the study hall.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:11:2.english: That brings honor to its owner - So that I will not need to sit on the ground.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:12:1.english: Who wrapped me in a coat - It was [as] important to him as a coat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:1:1.hebrew: כמאן מצלינן האידנא על החולים כר' יוסי - דאמר אדם נדון בכל יום, דאילו למאן דאמר דנדון בראש השנה הוי תפלת שוא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:1:1.english: "In accordance with whom do we pray nowadays for the sick? [In accordance with] Rabbi Yosei" - For he says [that] a person is judged every day; whereas according to the one who says that [a person] is judged on Rosh Hashanah, it would be a prayer in vain.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:2:1.hebrew: דלא כבבלאי דאכלי דייסא בנהמא - וא"כ, גם תבשיל עבה אסור לדידהו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:2:1.english: Not in accordance with the Babylonians, who eat porridge with bread - And if so, thick cooked food is also forbidden to them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:3:1.hebrew: איכא דמשאיל להני נקרני - פירוש: מי ימצא שישאל להני נקיי הדעת, כמו "נקיר שמיה" (פסחים קיא:), וכן "לנקר חצירו" (ביצה ח:). ויש מפרשין "נקדני", כמו (ברכות נ -) "הנקדנין תופסים אותו", ע"כ. וכל המדקד' בדברי' נקרא נקדן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:3:1.english: There are those who ask these fastidious people [nikranei] - Explanation: Who will be found to ask these refined [lit. clean-minded] people — like "Nakir is his name" (Pesachim 111b), and similarly "to clear [lenaker] his courtyard" (Beitzah 8b). And some explain [the reading as] nakdanei, as in (Berakhot 50): "The meticulous ones [hanakdanin] seize him" [end of quote]. And anyone who is meticulous in [his] matters is called a nakdan.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:4:1.hebrew: בחסיסי - קמח של קליות, וכן פר"י (פרק כל שעה ד' לט). ור"ח פירש: קמח של עדשים, ופירושו נראה יותר; דלפרש"י היה לו לקרותו "קימחא דאבישונא". ועוד אמר פ' כל שעה: "ממחו ליה קדרה בחסיסי"; ואי קימחא דאבשונא — הא אמר לעיל מיניה בההוא פירקא דאסור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:4:1.english: Baḥasisei [With ḥasisei] - Flour of toasted [grains], and so Rashi explained (Chapter Kol Sha'ah, daf 39[b]). And Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained: flour of lentils, and his explanation seems more [plausible]; for according to Rashi's explanation, it should have called it kimḥa d'avishuna. Furthermore, [the Gemara] says in Chapter Kol Sha'ah: "They stir a pot with ḥasisei"; and if [it were] kimḥa d'avishuna — didn't [the Gemara] say earlier in that same chapter that it is forbidden?

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:5:1.hebrew: לפלוט - כלומר: אם יצטרך לרוק, ירוק, ואל יניח בשביל כבוד רבו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:5:1.english: To spit out - That is to say, if he needs to spit, he should spit, and he should not refrain [from doing so] out of respect for his teacher.

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:7:2.hebrew: כל שכן דנסמוך עליהם למחר - שלא יתעכלו מהר, וכל זמן שהמאכל בתוך הבני מעיים, הלב נסעד:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:7:2.english: "All the more so that we can rely on them for tomorrow" - [Meaning] that they will not be digested quickly, and as long as the food is inside the intestines, the heart is sustained:

Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:9:1.hebrew: וחוגרני צדעי - פירוש: חוגר וקושר היה צדעיו, לפי שהיה חש בראשו על היין ששתה בפסח:
Tosafot on Nedarim 49b:9:1.english: "And I bind my temples" - Explanation: he would gird and bind his temples, because his head would ache from the wine that he drank on Passover.
